value.rationale: Probe-law sensitivity is a design issue for randomized correction of high-dimensional matrix-function traces. The result shows a stronger boundary than generic no-reduction warnings: the Frobenius residual becomes negligible relative to the inverse, the deterministic trace approximation becomes relatively accurate, and yet a single sparse offdiagonal mode drives a sign-probe variance explosion. The precise 3-level construction and two-level conditioning barrier explain why a Frobenius-only criterion can mislead Rademacher variance design. No runtime or finite-tolerance solver benefit is claimed.
